# Exact own-source payment at an exposed complete base

This note supplies a concrete transfer for the new outward-smoothed H problem. It uses the actual singleton sources proved in \`candidate 54bd04196c016a99\`. It also distinguishes being exposed in the deepest-base hull from being exposed in the complete sampled-base hull; only the latter is sufficient for the construction below.

## 1. A globally admissible field isolating one actual source

Let \(p\) be an exposed vertex of \(\operatorname{conv}P\), where \(P\) is the complete finite sampled base. Let \(Y=(p,y)\) be an interior source of its positive \(d\)-fiber \(K_p\). Let

\[
P_y(x)=1+a_y\cdot(x-y)>0\quad(x\in K_p)
\]

be its attained ordinary projective-energy normalizer. Thus the projective image \((K_p-y)/P_y\) has centroid zero. Write \(E_y=\int_{K_p}P_y^{-d-1}\,dx\), and \(h_y(n)=h_{K_p}(n)-n\cdot y>0\).

Choose an affine base gap \(g\) with \(g(p)=0\) and \(g(z)>0\) at every other sampled base. On \(K_p\), the desired normal-dependent convex field is

\[
F(n,x)=h_y(n)P_y(x)^{-d}.
\]

Here is an explicit globally finite convex extension. Let \(0<l\leq P_y\leq u<\infty\) on \(K_p\), and define

\[
J(s)=\max\!\left(0,\ \sup_{t\in[l,u]}
 \{t^{-d}-d\,t^{-d-1}(s-t)\}\right).
\]

This is globally finite, continuous, nonnegative and convex; it equals \(s^{-d}\) on \([l,u]\) by the supporting-line inequality and the tangent at \(t=s\). Set \(F(n,x)=h_y(n)J(P_y(x))\) globally. For each fixed \(n\), it is convex in the full physical coordinates; joint continuity follows from compactness of \([l,u]\).

The old body is compact and the finite nonzero gaps have a positive minimum. Hence one finite \(T\) makes

\[
\Phi_p(n,z,x)=[F(n,x)-Tg(z)]_+
\tag{1}
\]

vanish on every other measured fiber boundary. It agrees with \(h_y(n)P_y^{-d}\) on the own boundary. Equation (1) is globally finite, continuous and nonnegative, and convex in \((z,x)\) for each \(n\). It is therefore an actual allowed physical field. This is an exact finite construction, not an approximation that might leak onto another fiber.

The projective cone-change formula gives

\[
\int\Phi_p\,d\sigma=dE_y>0,
\tag{2}
\]

where \(\sigma\) is the sum of the actual fiber surface measures.

## 2. Exact payment for the actual smooth source menu

Take any actual menu at \(Y\), and let its nonnegative response weights \(\theta_j\) sum to one. Its boundary capture profile is

\[
W_p(z,x)=\sum_j\theta_j
 \Psi\!\left(
 \frac{N_j\cdot((z,x)-Y)+\epsilon f_H(Y)\Gamma(u_j)}
      {\delta\Gamma(u_j)}
 \right).
\]

On its own fiber, every summand dominates \(1_{\{u_j\cdot(x-y)\geq0\}}\), because the smoothing is outward and the buffer is nonnegative. The through-\(y\) plane is sent by the projective map to a through-zero plane with the same side.

Ordinary Grünbaum for the centroid of the projective image gives at least the fraction \(\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d\) of its volume on that side. Radial integration expresses that volume as the corresponding fraction of projective cone surface measure. Consequently every summand, and then their weighted average, satisfies

\[
\int \Phi_p W_p\,d\sigma\geq\Gamma_d\,dE_y
 =\Gamma_d\int\Phi_p\,d\sigma.
\tag{3}
\]

The inequality includes closed cuts and is exact for every \(\epsilon,\delta\geq0\) for which the source and normalizer exist. There is no smoothing loss in this own-source credit.

## 3. Combining actual singleton groups

Suppose all \(k\) smooth deepest source bases are exposed vertices of the complete base hull. Normalize each field from (1) to have integral one, and sum them. For the resulting nonnegative field \(\Phi\), positivity of every other contribution yields, for each source profile,

\[
\int \Phi W_i\,d\sigma\geq\Gamma_d,\qquad
\int\Phi\,d\sigma=k.
\]

Thus every profile has common efficiency at least \(\Gamma_d/k\). Any positive mixture of these profiles has the same lower bound. In particular, if the actual smooth separator gives a positive boundary law with capture part \(\sum_i\omega_iW_i\) and domination coefficient \(B_*\), testing with this \(\Phi\) proves

\[
B_*\geq\Gamma_d/k.
\]

The smooth parity theorem gives \(k\leq2^n\). Actual buffer-response corrections in \(B_*\), and their limiting control, must still be supplied by that separator theorem.

## 4. Why the deepest-base hull alone is insufficient

The smooth parity theorem makes every source a vertex of \(\operatorname{conv}I\). It does not make it a vertex of \(\operatorname{conv}P\). If \(p\in\operatorname{conv}(P\setminus\{p\})\), there is no affine gap \(g\) positive at all other sampled bases and zero at \(p\). Equation (1) cannot then isolate the whole own fiber by this argument. No substitute exposure is inferred from parity or from the smooth cap kernel having base centroid \(p\).

## 5. The unlocalized canonical chart has an actual obstruction

Take the sharp product body \(C=[0,1]^n\times D\), with \(D\) a simplex and \(N=2^n\geq2\). Every base is an actual smooth deepest base: an ambient cap contains at least its own smooth fiber contribution, while a sufficiently large finite exposing base tilt exactly isolates that same contribution. Thus mixed smooth depth on a fiber equals its own smooth depth, and all fibers have identical maxima. Symmetry and the convex depth region put the continuous source at the simplex centroid.

At that source the projective normalizer is \(P_y=1\): the derivative of the strictly convex energy integral vanishes at zero because \(y\) is the centroid. The constant global energy-root and volume-root supergradients therefore yield the canonical global chart \(R=1\). Its physical field is \(h_y(n)\) on EVERY fiber.

For one source, choose the actual smooth minimizing menu with finite exposing tilts that make every other fiber's integrand identically zero. Its kernel-weighted base centroid is exactly the source base. If \(Q_{\epsilon,\delta}\) is the common own smooth cap mass, integration by parts on the own fiber gives, for each menu cap,

\[
\int_{\partial D}h_y(n)\Psi(\cdots)\,dS
 =dQ_{\epsilon,\delta}
 +\int_D\frac{\psi(\cdots)}{\delta\Gamma(u)}
       u\cdot(x-y)\,dx
 \leq dQ_{\epsilon,\delta}.
\]

The last sign is exact: wherever the kernel is nonzero,
\(u\cdot(x-y)\in[-(\epsilon f_H+\delta)\Gamma(u),
-\epsilon f_H\Gamma(u)]\).
The denominator of the global constant chart is \(Nd|D|\). Its individual efficiency is therefore at most

\[
\frac{Q_{\epsilon,\delta}}{N|D|}
\longrightarrow\frac{\Gamma_d}{N}
\quad\text{as }\epsilon,\delta\downarrow0.
\]

For small positive parameters this is strictly below \(\Gamma_d\). Thus a global canonical chart cannot replace the localization step, even for an actual compatible body, actual smooth maximizing marks, distinct source parities, and exact per-cap kernel base centroids. This example does not assert that the displayed body is a global minimizer of the positive-parameter body objective. The localized construction in Sections 1--3 does pay it exactly.

## 6. Stronger transfer under strict full ambient exposure

The complete-base-vertex condition can be replaced by the following weaker normal-dependent condition. For every continuous unit normal \(n\), suppose there is an affine base slope \(a_n\) such that

\[
h_{K_p}(n)-h_{K_z}(n)-a_n\cdot(z-p)>0
\quad\text{for every }z\in P\setminus\{p\}.
\tag{4}
\]

The same slope is feasible for all neighboring normals, with a smaller positive margin, by continuity of the finitely many support functions. Compactness of the normal sphere gives a finite cover of such neighborhoods. A continuous partition of unity subordinate to this cover, and the corresponding convex combination of the finitely many chosen slopes, give a bounded continuous map \(a(n)\) and a single \(\eta>0\) such that the left side of (4), with \(a(n)\), is at least \(\eta\) for all \(z\ne p\).

Set

\[
g_n(z,x)=h_{K_p}(n)-n\cdot x-a(n)\cdot(z-p).
\]

This is affine in the physical point and jointly continuous in the normal. It is nonnegative on the canonical convex body, zero on the own exposed face with normal \(n\), and at least \(\eta\) on every other measured fiber. For the same finite convex extension \(F\) from Section 1, define

\[
\Phi_p(n,z,x)=[F(n,x)-Tg_n(z,x)]_+.
\tag{5}
\]

Choose finite \(T\) larger than the uniform bound of \(F/\eta\) on the other measured bundles. Then (5) vanishes there. At a regular boundary point of \(K_p\), evaluated at its actual own normal, \(g_n=0\), so (5) equals the desired projective cone field exactly. No assertion that it equals that field at unrelated normal/point pairs is needed. Equations (2)--(3) and their finite-sum consequence are unchanged.

Two sufficient geometric cases are explicit:

* If the original ambient body is strictly convex and all sampled fibers are positive, every sampled base is interior to its real projection: a positive boundary fiber would put a nontrivial segment on the ambient boundary. For fixed \(n\), the finite support-roof supergradient at that interior base supplies a full ambient supporting plane. Strict convexity makes its contact unique, hence separated from every other compact sampled fiber. This gives (4).
* For a finite compatible family, replace its support heights by \(h_{K_z}(n)+t(R-\|z\|^2)\), with \(t>0\) and \(R\) sufficiently large. This corresponds to actual Minkowski addition of the indicated positive-radius ball in every fiber, and remains compatible by concavity of \(R-\|z\|^2\). At \(p\), an affine support majorant of the old heights plus the tangent of this concave quadratic has strict excess at every other \(z\) of at least \(t\|z-p\|^2\). Thus (4) holds, even when the own continuous bodies have flat facets.

The conclusion concerns an ACTUAL stationary family satisfying (4). Approximating a general stationary family by either sufficient class does not preserve stationarity or its separator. Furthermore the isolating constant \(T\) can diverge as the strict support gap closes. Therefore this extension supplies no limiting argument for a general attained minimum. That obstruction remains explicit.
